import math

# Treasury Tax and Loan Account - Monthly Average Balance for 1961 (in millions of dollars)
treasury_balance = {
    'January': 3414,
    'February': 3812,
    'March': 3705,
    'April': 2171,
    'May': 3765,
    'June': 3572,
    'July': 3739,
    'August': 4581,
    'September': 4277,
    'October': 5924,
    'November': 4873,
    'December': 3869
}

# Monthly U.S. unemployment rate for 1961 (as percent, seasonally adjusted)
# Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
unemployment_rate = {
    'January': 6.4,
    'February': 6.4,
    'March': 6.9,
    'April': 7.0,
    'May': 7.0,
    'June': 7.1,
    'July': 7.3,
    'August': 6.7,
    'September': 6.7,
    'October': 6.6,
    'November': 6.5,
    'December': 6.2
}

# Create ordered lists
months = ['January', 'February', 'March', 'April', 'May', 'June', 
          'July', 'August', 'September', 'October', 'November', 'December']

x = [treasury_balance[m] for m in months]  # Treasury balance
y = [unemployment_rate[m] for m in months]  # Unemployment rate

print("Data for correlation calculation:")
print("Month | Treasury Balance (M$) | Unemployment Rate (%)")
print("-" * 55)
for m in months:
    print(f"{m:10} | {treasury_balance[m]:20} | {unemployment_rate[m]}")

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
n = len(x)
mean_x = sum(x) / n
mean_y = sum(y) / n

# Calculate deviations
dev_x = [xi - mean_x for xi in x]
dev_y = [yi - mean_y for yi in y]

# Calculate covariance
covariance = sum(dev_x[i] * dev_y[i] for i in range(n)) / n

# Calculate standard deviations
std_x = math.sqrt(sum(dx * dx for dx in dev_x) / n)
std_y = math.sqrt(sum(dy * dy for dy in dev_y) / n)

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
pearson_r = covariance / (std_x * std_y)

print(f"\nMean Treasury Balance: {mean_x:.2f}")
print(f"Mean Unemployment Rate: {mean_y:.2f}")
print(f"Std Dev Treasury Balance: {std_x:.2f}")
print(f"Std Dev Unemployment Rate: {std_y:.2f}")
print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {pearson_r:.4f}")
print(f"Rounded to 2 decimal places: {round(pearson_r, 2)}")
EOF
